To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
T3 acts on UCP3 in skeletal muscles to correct the cold intolerance of the mice with β-less adrenoceptors.
UCP3 plays a role in the thermogenic action of T3, and that the thermogenic effects in the absence of β-adrenergic receptors are mediated by the UCP3.
the thermogenic effects in vivo of 3,3′,5-triiodothyronine (T3) on skeletal muscle are dependent on UCP3.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new molecular targets of T3 action on energy metabolism.
the identification of new targets of the thyroid hormone action on thermogenesis and energy balance.
the molecular mechanisms by which T3 regulates the energy balance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
T3 is not only a permissive hormone for BAT thermogenesis, but also a direct stimulator of energy expenditure via a UCP3-mediated effect.
UCP3 is involved in the thermogenic effect of T3 in the muscle of mice.
T3 acts via UCP3 in muscle, which is the most active tissue during the dark period.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the β-less mice, that are cold intolerant, can be rescued by T3, and that UCP3, that is expressed in skeletal muscle, participates in the T3 effect.
UCP3 is not the main thermogenic target of T3, but it is a molecular determinant of T3 effects on energy metabolism.
the β-less mouse is a model for the study of UCP3 function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the thermogenic effect of T3 is not restricted to the BAT but is also exerted in skeletal muscle.
UCP3 is a new molecular target of T3 action on energy metabolism.
UCP3 is a target of thyroid hormone action and that its expression is regulated by thyroid hormones.
